elements.element: Maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14(a) requires commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence.

elements.element: Maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
Maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14(b) requires professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000.

elements.element: If the vendor processes Customer Data, maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition is triggered because Cellco handles Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information of Obligors. Section 10.14(c) requires $5,000,000 of cyber liability insurance covering that handling, including the personally identifiable information.

elements.element: Maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14(d) requires workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law.

elements.element: Provide certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The final sentence requires Cellco to provide certificates of insurance to the Issuer and Depositor on request.

elements.element: Maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14(b) requires $2,000,000, exceeding the fallback $1,000,000 requirement.

elements.element: If the vendor processes Customer Data, maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition is triggered because Cellco handles Receivable Files and Obligor personally identifiable information. Section 10.14(c) requires $5,000,000 of cyber liability coverage for that handling, exceeding the fallback $2,000,000 requirement.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement and therefore also satisfies the fallback limits. It is not minimal because it additionally requires all coverage to continue for one year after the agreement ends and expressly imposes the expense on Cellco, neither of which is required by the stated positions. The added covenant otherwise leaves the existing access and review provisions effective and introduces no apparent contradiction.
